section_title: How can fearing God help His friends face human threats?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 4 I tell you, My friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more. 5 But I will show you whom you should fear: Fear the One who, after you have been killed, has authority to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, fear Him!

6 Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God. 7 And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.

context_lines: Jesus addresses His hearers as friends and tells them not to be ruled by fear of people who can kill the body. He directs their fear toward the One whose authority reaches beyond death and into final judgment.

Then He turns to sparrows sold for a small price. God forgets none of them, and even the hairs on the disciples’ heads are numbered. The warning about God’s authority stands beside the assurance of His detailed care.

The passage does not deny the possibility of human violence; Jesus names it directly. He gives His friends a reason to remain faithful under its threat: people do not have the final word, and God does not lose sight of them.
common_interpretation_lines: Christian readings commonly hold together reverence for God’s authority and trust in His care. Wesley explicitly joins fear with trust in his notes on these verses, and the Catholic bishops’ notes understand the sayings as encouragement for followers facing persecution. ([Wesley on Luke 12:4–7](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-gospel-according-to-st-luke/); [USCCB note on Luke 12:2–9](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/luke/12))
god_plan_lines: Romans gives the wider ground for this confidence: God has given His Son, raised Him, and Christ intercedes for His people. Paul names persecution, danger and death, yet declares that none can separate them from God’s love in Christ. The care Jesus describes reaches beyond being spared every immediate harm to belonging to God through whatever comes. ([Romans 8:31–39](https://biblehub.com/bsb/romans/8.htm))
current_position_lines: We don't have a position on this passage yet. When our study reaches a conclusion the text supports, it will appear here.
